title: Keeping a Massachusetts Facility Licensed and Open to Inspection
topic: Facility licensure / Renewal, provisional credentials, inspection, nuclear pharmacies, wholesale distributors and non-resident pharmacies
subtopic: The drug store permit and its renewal under M.G.L. c. 112, ss. 38 and 39 and 247 CMR 6.04(8) and (9), 6.05 and 6.18; provisional pharmacy licences under 247 CMR 6.17; the provisional outsourcing facility registration, its limits, conversion and renewal under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 36E and 247 CMR 21.02, 21.03, 21.05 and 21.09; Board inspection, self-inspection and plans of correction under 247 CMR 9.19(21), 9.24 and 9.25; the nuclear pharmacy permit, radiopharmaceutical service, qualified nuclear pharmacist and change duties under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39B and 247 CMR 13.00; the wholesale drug licence, its changes, qualifications and inspection under M.G.L. c. 112, ss. 36A to 36C and 247 CMR 7.02 to 7.04; and the non-resident Drug Store Pharmacy license under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39J and 247 CMR 6.02(4) and 6.09(1) and (4)
learning_objectives: State when a Drug Store Pharmacy license, a non-resident Drug Store Pharmacy license, a nuclear pharmacy permit, an outsourcing facility registration and a wholesale drug licence each expire or must be renewed.
List what a pharmacy licence renewal under 247 CMR 6.04(9) requires and explain why renewal is a discretionary Board decision.
Say what the statutes and regulations do and do not provide for a Drug Store Pharmacy license that passes its expiry date.

Compare the provisional pharmacy licence under 247 CMR 6.17 with the provisional outsourcing facility registration under 247 CMR 21.03 on eligibility, permitted activity, end date, conversion and renewal.
Describe the Board's inspection authority, the pharmacy's document and self-inspection duties, and the plan of correction that follows a cited violation.
Apply the qualification, staffing, record and change-reporting requirements for a nuclear pharmacy and a qualified nuclear pharmacist.
Apply the per-location licence, annual renewal, 30-day change report, qualification factors and inspection terms for a Massachusetts wholesale drug distributor.
Explain the Massachusetts licence a non-resident pharmacy needs before dispensing or shipping to Massachusetts patients, and the duties of its designated pharmacist in charge.

orientation.text: A Massachusetts pharmacy exists legally because the Board has registered it and issued a permit, and that permit has an end date. M.G.L. c. 112, s. 38 provides that no store, retail food store pharmacy department or retail store pharmacy department shall be kept open for the transaction of the retail drug business, or be advertised or represented as transacting it with words such as drug store, pharmacy, apothecary, drug, drugs or medicine shop, unless it is registered with the Board and a permit has been issued; the only relief is written Board permission to use those words where no registered store exists in the town or voting precinct, and town does not include city. Section 38 also requires the permit to be displayed in a conspicuous place in the store or department for which it is issued. Section 39 lets the Board register the store and issue a permit to keep it open to the person it deems qualified, lets it refuse where the store would be inconsistent with or opposed to the best interests of the public health, welfare or safety, bars a permit to a corporation unless management is in the hands of a registered pharmacist, and requires a final decision within 150 days after the application is filed. Unlike the nuclear pharmacy statute, s. 39 does not say that a missed decision counts as approval.

The permit runs on a fixed two-year calendar that belongs to the facility, not to any pharmacist working there. Under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39 the permit expires on December 31 of each uneven numbered year following the date of its issue, and 247 CMR 6.05(2) says the same thing of a Drug Store Pharmacy license in the words December 31st of each odd numbered year following the date of its issuance; 247 CMR 6.05(1) sends renewal to 247 CMR 6.04(9). That paragraph makes renewal a Board decision rather than a formality. A duly authorized representative of the pharmacy applies in the form and manner the Board determines, fully and properly completed and submitted in a timely manner; the licensee pays a non-refundable fee set by the Executive Office of Administration and Finance; the application carries an attestation that the pharmacy complied with all mandatory reporting under 247 CMR 20.00 during the licensing period; and the Board may renew if it finds, in its reasonable discretion, that the licensee and any interest holder are suitable and renewal is consistent with the best interest of public health, welfare and safety. 247 CMR 6.04(8) adds that a pharmacy license is non-transferrable, and 247 CMR 6.18 bars denial of renewal on account of a complaint, charge, conviction, judgment, discipline or sanction arising from legally protected reproductive or gender-affirming health care that would have been lawful in Massachusetts and is consistent with good professional practice there. Fee amounts are not taught here, and the pharmacist's own biennial registration is a separate cycle covered with pharmacist licensure.

Neither M.G.L. c. 112, ss. 38 and 39 nor 247 CMR 6.00 states a grace period, a late-renewal procedure or a reinstatement procedure for a Drug Store Pharmacy license that is allowed to pass its December 31 expiry. What the texts do say is that the permit expires on that date and that s. 38 forbids keeping a store open for the retail drug business unless a permit has been issued. Read together, the course that is safe on any reading is to treat an expired permit as no permit and to have the renewal application in, and granted, before December 31 rather than to keep trading while the paperwork catches up. That is an inference from the two provisions, not a sentence either of them contains. Discipline, including any Board action against a facility licence, belongs to the Board discipline material; changes of name, ownership, location or Manager of Record and remodelling belong to the pharmacy change filings; and closure has its own section.

A provisional licence under 247 CMR 6.17 is a bridge for an applicant that is close to ready, and every term of it is short. The Board may, in its discretion, issue one in lieu of a sterile compounding, complex non-sterile compounding, institutional sterile compounding, non-resident Drug Store, non-resident sterile compounding or non-resident complex non-sterile compounding pharmacy license, provided the applicant submitted a complete application for that licence and demonstrated to the Board's satisfaction that it is in substantial compliance with Massachusetts pharmacy law and has the potential to achieve full compliance within the provisional period. A resident Drug Store Pharmacy license is not on the list. The provisional licence is valid until the earliest of three events: the Board converts it to the full licence, it is surrendered, suspended or revoked, or one year has passed since issue. The Board may convert it when it has determined the pharmacy is in full compliance, and 247 CMR 6.17(4) states flatly that a provisional license may not be renewed or extended. So substantial compliance opens the door, full compliance is what conversion needs, and one year is the outer wall. The compounding licences themselves, their applications and their inspections are taught with compounding operations.

The provisional outsourcing facility registration in 247 CMR 21.03 works differently and must not be merged with the provisional pharmacy licence. It exists because a full registration requires proof of an FDA inspection connected with the facility's section 503B registration within the two years immediately preceding the application, as M.G.L. c. 112, s. 36E(b) and 247 CMR 21.02(3)(e) both require. Where a Massachusetts applicant was not so inspected, the Board may issue a provisional registration if the application is otherwise complete; a non-resident outsourcing facility is not eligible for one at all. The holder may compound sterile drug preparations but may not distribute or dispense a sterile drug preparation within or outside the Commonwealth until it has been inspected by the FDA and has received a Massachusetts outsourcing facility registration. The two texts do not use the same verbs: M.G.L. c. 112, s. 36E(b) says only that the provisional registrant may not distribute a sterile drug preparation until it has been inspected, while 247 CMR 21.03(3) says it may not distribute or dispense one until inspected by the FDA and registered in Massachusetts. The regulation adds dispensing to the statute's bar, so a provisional registrant may neither distribute nor dispense. The provisional registration ends at the earliest of conversion, surrender, suspension or revocation, or expiry on December 31st of the first odd numbered year following issuance. The Board may convert it on proof of an FDA inspection under section 503B, provided the results are not grounds for denial under s. 36E(e). Both the full and the provisional registration are non-transferrable.

Two details of the outsourcing timetable decide questions. First, 247 CMR 21.03(6) allows a provisional outsourcing facility registration issued on or after September 1st of an odd numbered year to be renewed, and says that no other provisional outsourcing registration may be renewed or extended. That carve-out only has work to do if a registration issued in the autumn of an odd-numbered year would otherwise expire on December 31st of that same year, so the structure of the regulation supports reading the first odd numbered year following issuance as the first December 31st of an odd-numbered year that falls after the issue date; the text does not say so in terms, and the safe course is to plan on the earlier expiry. Second, a full registration, resident or non-resident, expires on December 31st of each odd numbered year following issuance under s. 36E(d) and 247 CMR 21.05, and renewal requires proof of a valid, current FDA 503B registration, payment and anything else the Board requires, not a fresh FDA inspection. Separately, 247 CMR 21.09(4) and (5) require a registrant to notify the Board in writing within 14 days of an FDA inspection and of receipt of an FDA Form 483 or Warning Letter. What section 503B itself requires of an outsourcing facility is federal compounding law, taught in its own section.

Inspection is the Board's standing check on every one of these credentials, and the pharmacy's duties when it happens are short. Under 247 CMR 9.24(1) the Board or its designees may visit any pharmacy licensed by the Board at any time without prior notice and inspect the pharmacy staff, activities and records to determine compliance with the laws and regulations governing the practice of pharmacy, and under 9.24(3) the pharmacy shall provide all documents requested by the Board or its designees in connection with an inspection or investigation. Under 9.24(2) all costs associated with inspections of non-resident pharmacies are paid by the non-resident pharmacy or applicant. The pharmacy also inspects itself: 247 CMR 9.19(21) requires a self-inspection within seven days of any renovation, expansion, relocation or change of Manager of Record, and at least one time per year, using a Board-approved inspection tool for routine compliance, sterile compounding and non-sterile compounding as applicable, and the completed tool is retained for at least two years. Those four events are the whole list of triggers the paragraph names. The self-inspection duty is not among the provisions that 9.19(23) disapplies for non-resident pharmacies or that 9.19(24) disapplies for institutional sterile compounding pharmacies.

What follows a cited violation is a written plan with its own clocks. Under 247 CMR 9.25(1) a pharmacy shall submit to the Board a written plan of correction for each violation cited in a statement of deficiency or inspection report, within 21 days or in the timeframe directed by the Board, in the manner and format the Board specifies. The plan describes the corrective action for each cited violation, the expected completion or implementation date and the individual or individuals responsible for each action, and under 9.25(3) it is signed by the Manager of Record and, if applicable, by the licensee who supervises the Manager of Record's practice of pharmacy. The pharmacy shall achieve compliance in the most expeditious manner possible, so the plan's completion dates are not a licence to wait. A plan that does not meet the requirements of the relevant 247 CMR section is considered unacceptable, returned, and must be resubmitted in revised form within seven days. The regulation does not say from what event the 21 days are counted, so the safe course is to count them from the date of the statement of deficiency or inspection report; the seven-day period arises only after a plan has been returned.

A nuclear pharmacy is licensed under its own statute, M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39B, and not as an ordinary Drug Store. It may not perform any pharmacy functions other than dispensing radiopharmaceutical drug products. The Board may deny registration on public-interest grounds and may not issue a permit to a corporation unless management is in the hands of a registered pharmacist, and for a corporation 247 CMR 13.03(9) asks that the nuclear pharmacy be managed and operated by a registered pharmacist in good standing with the Board. The permit expires on December 31 of each uneven numbered year following issuance under s. 39B and 247 CMR 13.04, and renewal is made on the Board's renewal form, fully and properly completed, submitted in a timely manner and accompanied by the required payment. The statute's decision rule is stronger than the Drug Store rule: the Board shall decide within 150 days of filing, and a failure to decide, except where the applicant's own delay causes it, constitutes approval and the permit shall be issued. Radiopharmaceutical service is defined in 247 CMR 13.02 to reach counting, dispensing, labeling and delivery, participation in selection and utilization reviews, safe storage and distribution, quality assurance and advice on therapeutic values, hazards and use, and an initial permit is sought on a completed Board application with the required payment under 247 CMR 13.03(1) and (2).

The people who run a nuclear pharmacy carry qualifications of their own. A qualified nuclear pharmacist, as 247 CMR 13.02 defines the term, is registered as a pharmacist under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24, employed in a nuclear pharmacy, has submitted satisfactory evidence of the required education, training and experience, and has received from the Board an official letter finding the pharmacist qualified. 247 CMR 13.06 sets the requirements: current registration; 200 contact hours of formal academic training in radiopharmaceutical preparation and handling, of which no more than 60 may be laboratory training; in addition, at least three months full-time or 500 hours of actual on-the-job experience under a qualified nuclear pharmacist in a nuclear pharmacy, or in a structured nuclear pharmacy training program of a Board-approved college or school of pharmacy; and a detailed affidavit of experience and training. Under 247 CMR 13.05 only a qualified nuclear pharmacist may be employed to direct and manage the pharmacy, only designated qualified nuclear pharmacists conduct its radiopharmaceutical activities, and one must be in personal attendance and on the premises whenever it is open. The same section keeps it inspectable and current: acquisition and disposition records for every radiopharmaceutical are kept readily retrievable for at least three years and available to the Board or its agents on request; the permit and the full-time pharmacists' registration certificates are posted conspicuously; a move needs a new permit application in advance, and operation at the new site waits for Board approval, a new permit and a new controlled substances registration; structural plans for establishment, remodelling or relocation go to the Board first; and the start or end of any pharmacist's employment is reported within ten days.

Wholesale distribution has a separate licence on a separate calendar. M.G.L. c. 112, s. 36A, subject to s. 35, forbids selling, distributing or delivering drugs or medicines at wholesale within the commonwealth without a licence; under s. 36B the licence goes only to an applicant actually engaged in and carrying on the wholesale business, is renewed on or before December first of each year, and must be obtained for each location, as 247 CMR 7.02(4) repeats. 247 CMR 7.02(5) lists what the Board collects at initial licensing and at every renewal: name, business address and telephone number, all trade or business names, the address, telephone number and contact person for each storage, handling and distribution facility, the type of ownership with the names of the people behind it, and whether controlled substances, legend drugs or over-the-counter drugs will be distributed. Under 7.02(6) any change in that information is submitted to the Board in writing within 30 days after the change. The qualifications follow in 7.02(7): in issuing, renewing or revoking a licence the Board considers at a minimum drug-distribution and controlled-substance convictions, any felony conviction, past manufacturing or distribution experience, false or fraudulent application material, sanctions on prior licences or registrations, compliance with prior licensing and record requirements, failure to control distribution, diversion, theft or loss, compliance with 247 CMR 7.00, and any other relevant factor; 7.02(8) reserves denial in the public interest; and 7.02(9) makes adequately educated, trained and experienced distribution staff a condition of receiving and retaining the licence. Board agents may inspect and investigate wholesale dealers, during business hours under s. 36C, and must give the licensee a copy of the inspection report within 15 days under 247 CMR 7.03(1); 7.04(9)(b) requires the distributor to let Board agents and authorized law enforcement officials enter and inspect premises and delivery vehicles and audit records and written procedures at reasonable times and in a reasonable manner. The wholesale controlled substance registration is taught elsewhere.

Massachusetts does license out-of-state pharmacies that serve Massachusetts patients, and not only compounding pharmacies. M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39J(a) directs the Board to establish a procedure to license non-resident pharmacies, defined in s. 39D as any pharmacy located outside the commonwealth that prescribes, ships, mails, sells or dispenses medications in the commonwealth. Section 39J(c) provides that no pharmacy or pharmacist operating outside the state shall prescribe, ship, mail, sell, transfer or dispense drug preparations in the commonwealth unless they are produced in a pharmacy granted a non-resident licence, and 247 CMR 6.02(4) provides that a pharmacy located outside Massachusetts may not dispense or ship any controlled substance into Massachusetts unless it holds a non-resident Drug Store Pharmacy license. The statute's words and the regulation's words are not identical, so the safe course for any out-of-state pharmacy that will dispense or ship medication to Massachusetts patients is to hold the non-resident Drug Store Pharmacy license first. A pharmacy shipping sterile or complex non-sterile compounded preparations needs the matching non-resident compounding licence as well, and under 247 CMR 9.20 a non-resident pharmacy complies with Massachusetts pharmacy law when filling, dispensing or shipping into Massachusetts unless otherwise specified; those compounding licences are taught with practice standards.

The non-resident Drug Store Pharmacy license has its own application, people and renewal terms. Under 247 CMR 6.09(1) the applicant submits the general application documentation in 247 CMR 6.04(2), proof of good standing from its home state dated within three months of the application submission date, and an inspection report from a Board approved inspector conducted within two years of that date; the Board may require an additional inspection by its agent or a Board approved inspector before final approval, and the applicant pays third-party inspector costs. A pharmacy dispensing or shipping any controlled substance into Massachusetts shall have a designated Massachusetts licensed pharmacist in charge, and M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39J(b) requires the designated pharmacist in charge to register with the Board, to be licensed and in good standing in the home state, and to answer for the pharmacy's compliance; that pharmacist reports the principal managers and a home-state good-standing letter annually and within 30 days after any change of office, corporate office or manager of record, and certifies the home-state licence and the keeping of records of drugs dispensed to Massachusetts patients, with an annual list of those drugs to the Board. A change of the Massachusetts licensed designated pharmacist in charge needs a Board application within 90 days of the previous pharmacist's termination or resignation under 247 CMR 6.09(4). The licence expires on December 31st of each odd numbered year following issuance, and renewal carries copies of all reports and correspondence about every state or federal inspection during the pending licensing period. Under s. 39J(e) the licence holder is subject to the prescription monitoring requirements of M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 24A, cannot obtain a waiver from them, cannot be approved without showing it can comply, and may lose the licence for failing to. The reporting duties of non-resident pharmacies under 247 CMR 20.00 are taught with quality-related events and reporting.

worked_examples.scenario: An out-of-state pharmacy that ships to Massachusetts patients received a provisional licence in lieu of a non-resident Drug Store Pharmacy license on February 10, 2026. Its owner has diarised December 31, 2027 as the expiry, reasoning that non-resident Drug Store licences expire on December 31 of an odd-numbered year, and plans to ask for a renewal then if full compliance is not yet reached.
steps: Identify the credential actually held. It is a provisional licence under 247 CMR 6.17, not a non-resident Drug Store Pharmacy license, so the odd-year expiry in 247 CMR 6.09(1)(d) does not govern it.

Apply 247 CMR 6.17(2): the provisional licence is valid until the earliest of conversion by the Board, surrender, suspension or revocation, or one year since the Board issued it. Without conversion it ends no later than February 10, 2027.
Apply 247 CMR 6.17(4): a provisional license may not be renewed or extended, so no renewal is available at any date.
Apply 247 CMR 6.17(3): the only way forward is conversion, which the Board may grant once it determines the pharmacy is in full compliance with Massachusetts pharmacy law.
worked_examples.resolution: The owner has borrowed the full licence's calendar. The provisional licence ends by February 10, 2027 at the latest and cannot be renewed or extended; the pharmacy needs a Board determination of full compliance and conversion before then.

worked_examples.scenario: Two Massachusetts outsourcing applicants lacked an FDA inspection in the two years before applying. Facility A received a provisional registration on October 5, 2025 and Facility B on March 3, 2026. Neither has been inspected by the FDA. Both want to know how long they have, whether they may renew, and whether they may ship compounded sterile preparations to local hospitals meanwhile.
steps: Fix the end date under 247 CMR 21.03(4)(c): December 31st of the first odd numbered year following issuance. For Facility B that is December 31, 2027. For Facility A the structure of 21.03(6) supports December 31, 2025, and that earlier date is the safe planning assumption.

Apply 247 CMR 21.03(6): a provisional registration issued on or after September 1st of an odd numbered year may be renewed. Facility A's October 5, 2025 registration qualifies; Facility B's March 3, 2026 registration may not be renewed or extended.

Apply 247 CMR 21.03(3) to both: each may compound sterile drug preparations but may not distribute or dispense a sterile drug preparation within or outside the Commonwealth until inspected by the FDA and holding a Massachusetts outsourcing facility registration.
Note the route out under 21.03(5): the Board may convert on proof of an FDA inspection under section 503B whose results are not grounds for denial under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 36E(e).
worked_examples.resolution: Only Facility A may renew, because only it was issued on or after September 1st of an odd-numbered year; neither may ship to hospitals, since compounding is allowed but distribution waits for an FDA inspection and a full Massachusetts registration.

worked_examples.scenario: A Board inspector makes an unannounced visit to a Massachusetts community pharmacy that relocated nine days earlier and issues an inspection report citing three violations. The staff pharmacist on duty declines to produce the self-inspection tool until the Manager of Record returns, and the Manager of Record later plans to send a plan of correction for the most serious violation only, in about a month, signed by the staff pharmacist.
steps: Under 247 CMR 9.24(1) and (3) the Board may inspect at any time without prior notice, and the pharmacy shall provide all documents requested in connection with the inspection; the absence of the Manager of Record is not a ground to withhold them.

Under 247 CMR 9.19(21) the relocation triggered a self-inspection within seven days of the relocation, using the Board-approved tool, in addition to the annual one, and the completed tool is kept for at least two years.

Under 247 CMR 9.25(1) a written plan of correction is owed for each of the three cited violations, within 21 days or the timeframe the Board directs, not only for the most serious one and not in about a month.

Under 247 CMR 9.25(3) the Manager of Record signs the plan, together with the licensee who supervises the Manager of Record's practice if applicable; under 9.25(5) a plan returned as unacceptable must be resubmitted within seven days.
worked_examples.resolution: Every step of the plan is wrong: the documents must be produced during the inspection, the relocation self-inspection was due within seven days, a plan is owed for all three violations within 21 days unless the Board sets another timeframe, and the Manager of Record must sign it.

worked_examples.scenario: A mail-order pharmacy located and licensed in another state wants to start sending prescription medications, including some controlled substances, to Massachusetts residents. Its owner believes a pharmacy licensed in its home state needs nothing from Massachusetts unless it compounds.
steps: Classify the pharmacy: under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39D it is a non-resident pharmacy, because it is located outside the commonwealth and ships, mails or dispenses medications in the commonwealth.

Apply the licence gates: 247 CMR 6.02(4) bars dispensing or shipping any controlled substance into Massachusetts without a non-resident Drug Store Pharmacy license, and M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39J(c) bars shipping or dispensing drug preparations in the commonwealth unless produced in a pharmacy granted a non-resident licence.

Assemble the application under 247 CMR 6.09(1): the 6.04(2) documentation, home-state good standing dated within three months, and a Board approved inspector's report from within two years, with the Board free to require an additional inspection at the applicant's cost.

Staff it: a designated Massachusetts licensed pharmacist in charge for controlled substance shipments under 6.09(1)(c), who under s. 39J(b) registers with the Board, is licensed and in good standing in the home state, and makes the annual and 30-day reports.
Confirm it can meet the prescription monitoring requirements of M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 24A, since under s. 39J(e) no waiver is available and the application will not be approved without that showing.
worked_examples.resolution: The owner is wrong: Massachusetts licenses non-resident pharmacies generally, and this pharmacy needs a non-resident Drug Store Pharmacy license, a designated pharmacist in charge and the ability to comply with s. 24A before it ships; compounding would only add a further licence.

worked_examples.scenario: A Massachusetts wholesale drug distributor licensed at one warehouse opens a second warehouse in another town and, in the same month, replaces the contact person listed for its existing facility. Its compliance officer proposes to cover the new site under the existing licence and to mention the new contact person at the next annual renewal.
steps: Under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 36B and 247 CMR 7.02(4) a person engaged in the wholesale drug business at more than one location obtains a licence for each location, so the second warehouse needs its own licence.
The contact person for each facility used for storage, handling and distribution is information required by 247 CMR 7.02(5)(c).
Under 247 CMR 7.02(6) a change in any 7.02(5) information is submitted to the Board in writing within 30 days after the change, so waiting for renewal on or before December first is not compliant.

At renewal, and on the new application, the Board weighs the 7.02(7) factors, which include any felony conviction and failure to control diversion, theft or loss, and it may deny a licence not in the public interest under 7.02(8).
worked_examples.resolution: Both proposals fail: the new warehouse needs its own licence, and the changed contact person must be reported in writing within 30 days after the change rather than held for the annual renewal.

worked_examples.scenario: A registered Massachusetts pharmacist with 210 contact hours of radiopharmaceutical coursework, 80 of them in the laboratory, and 400 hours of supervised work in a nuclear pharmacy is offered the post of directing a new nuclear pharmacy. The owner also assumes the pharmacy may fill ordinary retail prescriptions on the side.
steps: Under 247 CMR 13.05 only a qualified nuclear pharmacist may be employed to direct and manage the pharmacy, and 247 CMR 13.02 requires a Board official letter finding the pharmacist qualified.

Test the training under 247 CMR 13.06(2): 200 contact hours are needed with no more than 60 from laboratory training, so only 60 of the 80 laboratory hours count and 130 plus 60 gives 190 countable hours.

Test the experience under 13.06(3): three months full-time or 500 hours of on-the-job experience under a qualified nuclear pharmacist, and 400 hours falls short; a detailed affidavit is also required.
Under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39B the nuclear pharmacy shall not perform any pharmacy functions other than dispensing radiopharmaceutical drug products, so ordinary retail filling is outside its permit.
worked_examples.resolution: The pharmacist is not yet qualified, being short on countable academic hours because of the laboratory cap and short on experience, and cannot direct the pharmacy without the Board's letter; the retail side business is barred outright.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A Massachusetts Drug Store Pharmacy license expires on ______.
retrieval_prompts.answer: December 31 of each odd (uneven) numbered year following the date of issuance, under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39 and 247 CMR 6.05(2).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What attestation must accompany each pharmacy licence renewal application?
retrieval_prompts.answer: An attestation that the pharmacy complied with all mandatory reporting during that licensing period in accordance with 247 CMR 20.00 (247 CMR 6.04(9)(c)).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: True or false: the Board must renew a pharmacy licence once a complete application and fee are received.
retrieval_prompts.answer: False. Under 247 CMR 6.04(9)(d) the Board may renew if it finds, in its reasonable discretion, that the licensee and any interest holder are suitable and renewal is consistent with the best interest of public health, welfare and safety.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Within what period must the Board decide a drug store application, and what does the statute say if it misses that period?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Within 150 days after filing under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39; s. 39 attaches no deemed approval to a missed decision, unlike s. 39B for a nuclear pharmacy.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: List the three events that end a provisional pharmacy licence under 247 CMR 6.17.
retrieval_prompts.answer: Conversion by the Board to the full licence; surrender, suspension or revocation; or one year passing since issue, whichever occurs first. It may not be renewed or extended.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Can a resident Drug Store Pharmacy applicant receive a provisional licence under 247 CMR 6.17?
retrieval_prompts.answer: No such licence is listed: 6.17 reaches sterile, complex non-sterile, institutional sterile, non-resident Drug Store, non-resident sterile and non-resident complex non-sterile compounding licences only.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What may, and may not, the holder of a provisional outsourcing facility registration do?
retrieval_prompts.answer: It may compound sterile drug preparations but may not distribute or dispense a sterile drug preparation within or outside the Commonwealth until inspected by the FDA and holding a Massachusetts outsourcing facility registration (247 CMR 21.03(3)).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which provisional outsourcing facility registrations may be renewed?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Only one issued on or after September 1st of an odd numbered year; no other may be renewed or extended (247 CMR 21.03(6)).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Within how many days must an outsourcing facility registrant tell the Board of an FDA inspection or an FDA Form 483?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Within 14 days, in writing (247 CMR 21.09(4) and (5)).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Name the four events that trigger a pharmacy self-inspection within seven days, and the retention period for the tool.
retrieval_prompts.answer: Renovation, expansion, relocation or change of Manager of Record; the completed tool is kept for at least two years, and a self-inspection is also done at least once a year (247 CMR 9.19(21)).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A pharmacy receives an inspection report citing violations. What is due, by when, and who signs?
retrieval_prompts.answer: A written plan of correction for each cited violation within 21 days or the Board's directed timeframe, signed by the Manager of Record and, if applicable, the supervising licensee; a returned plan is revised within seven days (247 CMR 9.25).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Who pays for the inspection of a non-resident pharmacy?
retrieval_prompts.answer: The non-resident pharmacy or applicant pays all associated costs (247 CMR 9.24(2)).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: State the academic training and experience a qualified nuclear pharmacist needs.
retrieval_prompts.answer: 200 contact hours of formal academic training in radiopharmaceutical preparation and handling, no more than 60 of them laboratory, plus three months full-time or 500 hours of supervised on-the-job experience or a structured Board-approved school program, with a detailed affidavit (247 CMR 13.06).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Within how many days must a nuclear pharmacy report that a pharmacist has started or stopped working there?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Within ten days of the commencement or termination of employment (247 CMR 13.05).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: When is a Massachusetts wholesale drug licence renewed, and how many licences does a multi-site wholesaler need?
retrieval_prompts.answer: On or before December first of each year, with one licence for each location (M.G.L. c. 112, s. 36B; 247 CMR 7.02(4)).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A wholesale distributor changes information it reported under 247 CMR 7.02(5). What must it do?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Submit the change to the Board in writing within 30 days after the change (247 CMR 7.02(6)).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Does Massachusetts law require an out-of-state pharmacy that is not compounding to hold a Massachusetts licence before shipping to Massachusetts patients?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Yes. M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39J provides for non-resident pharmacy licences and bars dispensing drug preparations in the commonwealth without one, and 247 CMR 6.02(4) requires a non-resident Drug Store Pharmacy license to dispense or ship any controlled substance into Massachusetts.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A non-resident pharmacy's Massachusetts licensed designated pharmacist in charge resigns. What is the deadline?
retrieval_prompts.answer: An application for Board approval of the change within 90 days of the resignation (247 CMR 6.09(4)); the s. 39J(b)(1) report within 30 days after a change of manager of record may also be triggered.

quick_review.text: No store may be kept open for the retail drug business, or hold itself out as a pharmacy, without Board registration and a permit, and the permit is displayed conspicuously (M.G.L. c. 112, s. 38).

A Drug Store Pharmacy license expires on December 31 of each odd-numbered year following issuance; it is non-transferrable, and renewal turns on a timely application, fee, reporting attestation and a Board suitability finding.
No grace, late-renewal or reinstatement procedure for a pharmacy licence appears in ss. 38 and 39 or 247 CMR 6.00; renew before December 31.

A provisional pharmacy licence needs a complete application and substantial compliance, ends at conversion, surrender, suspension, revocation or one year, and may not be renewed or extended; 6.17 does not list a resident Drug Store Pharmacy license.

A provisional outsourcing registration is for Massachusetts applicants lacking a two-year FDA inspection; it allows compounding but not distribution or dispensing, and is renewable only if issued on or after September 1st of an odd-numbered year.
The Board may inspect a licensed pharmacy at any time without notice, and the pharmacy provides every document requested.
Self-inspection: yearly and within seven days of renovation, expansion, relocation or change of Manager of Record, with the tool kept two years.
Plan of correction: each cited violation, 21 days or as directed, signed by the Manager of Record; revised within seven days if returned.

A nuclear pharmacy holds a s. 39B permit expiring December 31 of uneven years, dispenses only radiopharmaceuticals, and is directed only by a Board-qualified nuclear pharmacist (200 hours, no more than 60 laboratory, plus three months or 500 hours of experience).
Wholesale licence: one per location, renewed on or before December first each year, changes to reported information in writing within 30 days.
An out-of-state pharmacy shipping medications to Massachusetts patients needs a non-resident Drug Store Pharmacy license, which expires on December 31st of odd-numbered years.

decision_logic.condition: The facts concern a credential's expiry or renewal.
decision_logic.action: Identify the credential first: Drug Store or non-resident Drug Store (odd-year December 31), nuclear pharmacy (uneven-year December 31), outsourcing facility (odd-year December 31st), wholesale drug licence (on or before December first each year), or a provisional licence or registration with its own end rule.

decision_logic.condition: A pharmacy asks whether its renewal is assured once it pays.
decision_logic.action: Check the 247 CMR 6.04(9) elements: authorized representative, timely and complete form, non-refundable fee, 247 CMR 20.00 reporting attestation, and a discretionary Board finding that licensee and interest holders are suitable; 6.18 removes legally protected health care activity as a ground of denial.

decision_logic.condition: The holder of a provisional licence or registration wants more time.
decision_logic.action: If it is a provisional pharmacy licence, the answer is no: one year at most, no renewal or extension, conversion only on full compliance. If it is a provisional outsourcing registration, check the issue date: renewal is possible only if issued on or after September 1st of an odd-numbered year.

decision_logic.condition: A provisional outsourcing registrant wants to supply product.
decision_logic.action: Refuse distribution or dispensing inside or outside the Commonwealth until an FDA inspection and a full Massachusetts registration; compounding may continue.

Admit the inspection without notice, produce every document requested, and, if violations are cited, calendar a plan of correction for each within 21 days or the directed timeframe, signed by the Manager of Record.

decision_logic.condition: The pharmacy renovates, expands, relocates or changes its Manager of Record.
decision_logic.action: Complete a Board-tool self-inspection within seven days of the event, whatever the date of the last annual one, and keep it two years; the change filings themselves are a separate matter.

decision_logic.condition: A pharmacy outside Massachusetts wants to serve Massachusetts patients.
decision_logic.action: Require a non-resident Drug Store Pharmacy license before dispensing or shipping, a designated pharmacist in charge meeting s. 39J(b), and demonstrated ability to comply with M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 24A; add the matching non-resident compounding licence for sterile or complex non-sterile compounded preparations.

decision_logic.condition: A wholesale distributor changes something or adds a site.
decision_logic.action: A new site needs its own licence; a change to 247 CMR 7.02(5) information goes to the Board in writing within 30 days after the change.

decision_logic.condition: Someone is to direct a nuclear pharmacy.
decision_logic.action: Confirm a Board official letter of qualification resting on current registration, 200 academic hours with no more than 60 laboratory, three months or 500 hours of supervised experience, and an affidavit.

ma_vs_federal.text: Massachusetts outsourcing facility registration rests on federal status: proof of a valid, current FDA registration under section 503B and, for a full registration, an FDA inspection within the two years immediately preceding the application. The Massachusetts registration is still a separate Board credential with its own term, renewal and notification duties, and federal registration alone does not satisfy them.

A provisional outsourcing registration becomes a full one only on proof of an FDA section 503B inspection, and the Board then asks whether the results are grounds for denial under Massachusetts law in M.G.L. c. 112, s. 36E(e).

exceptions.text: Under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 38 the words drug store, pharmacy and the like may be used for an unregistered store with the Board's written permission where no registered store exists in the town or voting precinct; town does not include city.

247 CMR 6.18 bars denial of a pharmacy's initial licensure or renewal on account of a complaint, charge, conviction, judgment, discipline or other sanction arising from legally protected reproductive or gender-affirming health care that would have been lawful in Massachusetts and is consistent with good professional practice there.
A provisional outsourcing facility registration issued on or after September 1st of an odd numbered year may be renewed, the single exception to the bar on renewing or extending one.
A non-resident outsourcing facility is not eligible for a provisional outsourcing registration.
The 21-day period for a plan of correction yields to any different timeframe the Board directs.
The 150-day deemed approval of a nuclear pharmacy application does not apply where the applicant's own delay causes the Board's failure to act.
A non-resident pharmacy holding a s. 39J licence cannot obtain a waiver from the prescription monitoring requirements of M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 24A.

timing_deadlines.timeframe: Expires December 31 of each odd-numbered year following issuance
timing_deadlines.consequence: The permit expires; the texts state no grace or late-renewal procedure, and s. 38 bars keeping a store open without a permit.

timing_deadlines.event: Board decision on a drug store application
timing_deadlines.consequence: The statute requires a final decision but attaches no deemed approval.

timing_deadlines.timeframe: At most one year from issue
timing_deadlines.consequence: Ends unless converted earlier; may not be renewed or extended.

timing_deadlines.timeframe: December 31st of the first odd-numbered year following issuance
timing_deadlines.consequence: Ends unless converted, surrendered, suspended or revoked earlier; renewable only if issued on or after September 1st of an odd-numbered year.

timing_deadlines.event: Outsourcing facility registration, resident or non-resident
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Expires December 31st of each odd-numbered year following issuance
timing_deadlines.consequence: Renewal requires proof of a valid, current FDA 503B registration and payment.

timing_deadlines.event: FDA inspection, FDA Form 483 or Warning Letter at an outsourcing facility
timing_deadlines.consequence: Written notice to the Board is owed.

timing_deadlines.event: Renovation, expansion, relocation or change of Manager of Record
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Self-inspection within seven days; also at least once a year
timing_deadlines.consequence: Completed Board-approved tool retained for at least two years.

timing_deadlines.event: Violation cited in a statement of deficiency or inspection report
timing_deadlines.timeframe: 21 days, or the timeframe the Board directs
timing_deadlines.consequence: A written plan of correction for each violation is due.

timing_deadlines.event: Plan of correction returned as unacceptable
timing_deadlines.consequence: A revised plan must be submitted.

timing_deadlines.timeframe: Expires December 31 of each uneven-numbered year following issuance
timing_deadlines.consequence: Renewal on the Board form with payment, submitted in a timely manner.

timing_deadlines.event: Board decision on a nuclear pharmacy application
timing_deadlines.consequence: Failure to decide, unless caused by the applicant's delay, is approval and the permit shall issue.

timing_deadlines.event: Pharmacist starts or stops working at a nuclear pharmacy
timing_deadlines.consequence: The nuclear pharmacy reports the employment or termination to the Board.

timing_deadlines.timeframe: On or before December first of each year
timing_deadlines.consequence: Renewal carries the 247 CMR 7.02(5) information and the Board weighs the 7.02(7) factors.

timing_deadlines.event: Change in wholesale information reported under 247 CMR 7.02(5)
Board inspection of a wholesale distributor
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Report copy within 15 days of the inspection
timing_deadlines.consequence: Board agents provide the licensee a copy of the inspection report.

timing_deadlines.event: Non-resident Drug Store Pharmacy license term
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Expires December 31st of each odd-numbered year following issuance
timing_deadlines.consequence: Renewal includes copies of all state or federal inspection reports and correspondence from the pending licensing period.

timing_deadlines.event: Change of office, corporate office or manager of record at a non-resident pharmacy
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Within 30 days after the change, and annually
timing_deadlines.consequence: The designated pharmacist in charge submits the s. 39J(b)(1) report with a home-state good-standing letter.

timing_deadlines.event: Termination or resignation of a non-resident pharmacy's Massachusetts licensed designated pharmacist in charge
timing_deadlines.consequence: An application for Board approval of the change is submitted.

forms_records.text: A pharmacy licence renewal is made in the form and manner the Board determines by a duly authorized representative of the pharmacy, fully and properly completed and submitted in a timely manner, with a non-refundable fee and an attestation of compliance with all mandatory reporting under 247 CMR 20.00 during the licensing period.
The drug store permit is displayed in a conspicuous place in the store or pharmacy department for which it is issued.
The completed Board-approved self-inspection tool, covering routine compliance and, as applicable, sterile and non-sterile compounding, is retained for at least two years.

A plan of correction is written, prepared in the manner and format the Board specifies, and states for each cited violation the corrective action, the expected completion or implementation date and the responsible individuals, with the signatures of the Manager of Record and, if applicable, the supervising licensee.

A non-resident Drug Store application carries the 247 CMR 6.04(2) documentation, home-state good standing dated within three months and a Board approved inspector's report from within two years; renewal carries copies of all state or federal inspection reports and correspondence from the pending licensing period.

A non-resident pharmacy's designated pharmacist in charge files a report naming the location, name and title of all principal managers with a home-state good-standing letter annually and within 30 days after a change of office, corporate office or manager of record, and the Board receives an annual list of drugs dispensed in the commonwealth.
An outsourcing facility renewal carries proof of a valid, current FDA 503B registration and payment; the Board receives written notice within 14 days of an FDA inspection, Form 483 or Warning Letter.

A nuclear pharmacy keeps detailed records of the acquisition and disposition of all radiopharmaceuticals in readily retrievable form for at least three years, available to the Board or its agents on request, posts its permit and full-time pharmacists' registration certificates, and renews on the Board's renewal form.
A qualified nuclear pharmacist submits a detailed affidavit of experience and training and holds the Board's official letter of qualification.

A wholesale distributor's application and renewal carry the 247 CMR 7.02(5) information; the application is signed by each applicant under oath before a notary public, and changes to that information are submitted in writing within 30 days.

role_duties.duty: Decide drug store applications within 150 days, renew pharmacy licences on a discretionary suitability finding, convert a provisional licence when it has determined full compliance and a provisional outsourcing registration on proof of an FDA inspection whose results are not grounds for denial, and inspect licensed pharmacies at any time without notice.

role_duties.role: Pharmacy licensee and its authorized representative
role_duties.duty: Apply for renewal in the Board's form and manner before expiry with the fee and the 247 CMR 20.00 reporting attestation, display the permit, provide every document requested during an inspection, and self-inspect annually and after the four trigger events.

Sign the plan of correction for each cited violation, together with the supervising licensee where applicable, and see that it reaches the Board within 21 days or the directed timeframe and is revised within seven days if returned.

role_duties.role: Non-resident pharmacy and its designated pharmacist in charge
role_duties.duty: Hold a non-resident Drug Store Pharmacy license before dispensing or shipping into Massachusetts; the pharmacist in charge registers with the Board, stays licensed and in good standing at home, makes the annual and 30-day reports, and certifies record-keeping; the pharmacy pays inspection costs, reports enforcement actions in any state, applies within 90 days on a change of pharmacist in charge, and complies with M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 24A.

Before full registration, compound without distributing or dispensing; keep the FDA 503B registration current for renewal; notify the Board within 14 days of an FDA inspection, Form 483 or Warning Letter.

Dispense only radiopharmaceutical drug products, employ only a qualified nuclear pharmacist to direct it, keep a qualified nuclear pharmacist in attendance whenever open, keep radiopharmaceutical records three years for Board inspection, obtain a new permit before operating at a new location, submit structural plans first, and report pharmacist hiring or departure within ten days.

Hold current registration, complete 200 academic hours with no more than 60 laboratory and three months or 500 hours of supervised experience, submit the affidavit and obtain the Board's letter of qualification.

License each location, renew on or before December first each year, report changes to 7.02(5) information within 30 days, staff distribution with adequately trained people, and admit Board agents and authorized officials to inspect premises and vehicles and audit records.

common_traps.text: Using the pharmacist's personal registration cycle for the facility. The Drug Store Pharmacy license runs to December 31 of an odd-numbered year and belongs to the facility.
Treating renewal as automatic on payment. 247 CMR 6.04(9)(d) makes it a discretionary Board decision on suitability, and the application carries a reporting attestation.
Assuming a provisional pharmacy licence can be extended while compliance work finishes. 247 CMR 6.17(4) forbids renewal and extension.

Carrying the pharmacy rule across to outsourcing. A provisional outsourcing registration issued on or after September 1st of an odd-numbered year may be renewed, and it ends on a December 31st date rather than one year after issue.

Reading the statute's bar on distributing as leaving dispensing open to a provisional outsourcing registrant. 247 CMR 21.03(3) bars distribution and dispensing alike until FDA inspection and full Massachusetts registration.
Reading permission to compound under a provisional outsourcing registration as permission to ship. Distribution and dispensing wait for an FDA inspection and a full Massachusetts registration.
Treating a recent annual self-inspection as covering a relocation. The relocation independently triggers a self-inspection within seven days.
Sending a plan of correction only for the worst violation, or having someone other than the Manager of Record sign it.
Assuming Massachusetts licenses only out-of-state compounding pharmacies. M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39J and 247 CMR 6.02(4) reach non-resident pharmacies generally.
Confusing the non-resident 30-day statutory report after a change of manager of record with the 90-day application after a change of designated pharmacist in charge.
Assuming one wholesale licence covers every warehouse, or that wholesale changes can wait for the annual December renewal.
Counting all laboratory hours toward the 200-hour academic requirement for a qualified nuclear pharmacist; no more than 60 count.
